newsitem.title: USA: NYS Senator urges Albany vote on future tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: NYS Senator urges Albany vote on future tax cuts.

text.p: State Sen Franz Leichter, D-Manhattan, Monday warned huge, five-year tax cuts contained in Albany's new budget plan could amount to "fiscal suicide," and urged that future cuts should voted on again.
Leichter cited a study by the Fiscal Policy Institute that he said found revenue losses in the fifth year of the new, 1998 fiscal budget were 35 times the amount in the first year.
The state senator's amendment would ensure no tax reduction or tax expenditure in the new tax bill would take effect without the affirmative vote of the legislature at the start of the year.
"The New York legislature is on the verge of committing fiscal suicide for the state," he said, in prepared remarks.

Noting fiscal monitors had attacked the new budget plan for back-loading tax reductions, he added "If the legislature goes forward with this plan, it will find that it will have no choice but to make draconian cuts in much needed health, welfare and education programs, or else raise taxes and go back on its promise to the taxpayers to this state."

The Senator also submitted a measure that would require future legislative appropriations bills to be itemized, and public hearings held on them. Such an itemized budget would set out the size and salary of legislative and administrative staffs, itemize non-personnel expenses, like rent, mailings and office supplies. He added the new budget raises the legislative budget by 2.0 percent to $180.57 million.
